title: Global News in Five Quick Slides

slides.headline: Global News in Five Quick Slides
slides.subtitle: Catch up on the world's most important headlines in under two minutes.

slides.headline: Border wall water drilling halted
slides.explanation: The Trump administration ordered crews to stop drilling wells for border wall construction in drought-hit New Mexico. This decision follows growing concerns about the impact on local water supplies.

slides.headline: Markets react to Iran talk claims
slides.explanation: US stocks are nearing record highs while oil prices dip following reports of potential talks with Iran. Washington and Tehran are currently providing conflicting accounts on whether these negotiations are actually happening.

slides.headline: States sue over new tariff plan
slides.explanation: A coalition of 25 states is suing the Trump administration over new trade tariffs. They argue the move is a workaround to re-impose levies that the Supreme Court previously ruled illegal.

slides.headline: Russian critic flees to France
slides.explanation: Prominent anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin has escaped to Paris amid a worsening crackdown on dissent in Russia. This comes as Moscow tightens control ahead of upcoming parliamentary elections.

slides.headline: Romania blasts rock to save power
slides.explanation: Romania used explosives to clear a rock from the Danube River to boost water flow for a nuclear plant. The move aims to keep the plant cool during a severe heatwave causing energy strain across Europe.

caption:
From rising stock markets to a dramatic escape in Russia, here are five stories shaping the world today. We break down the news so you can stay informed without the noise. Which of these updates surprised you the most?

title: Tech Update: AI Trips and Fitbit Fixes

slides.headline: Tech Update: AI Trips and Fitbit Fixes
slides.subtitle: Five quick stories to get you up to speed on the tech world today.

slides.headline: Game Freak is experimenting again
slides.explanation: The studio behind Pokémon is trying new things with its latest project, Beast of Reincarnation. It is a rare departure from their usual formula that shows the team is looking for new creative ground.

slides.headline: Fitbit finally talks to Apple Health
slides.explanation: Google is updating the Fitbit app to let you sync your health data directly with Apple Health. This makes it much easier to keep all your fitness tracking in one place without manual entry.

slides.headline: Palantir CEO criticizes AI labs
slides.explanation: Alex Karp says current AI companies are too untrustworthy for big businesses to rely on. His comments follow a very profitable quarter for his own company.

slides.headline: Snap CEO on the future of AR
slides.explanation: Evan Spiegel says mass adoption of consumer AR glasses is still years away, likely not happening until the end of the decade. He is keeping expectations realistic despite the hype surrounding the tech.

slides.headline: OpenAI trip faces online backlash
slides.explanation: OpenAI is facing criticism after hosting an influencer brand trip. People are questioning the optics of the event while tensions over AI safety and ethics remain high.
